summary: Top-down camera panning in two independent styles: edge pan and drag pan.
overview: Two panning styles in one component, each toggled separately. Edge pan is the MOBA and RTS default — push the cursor to the screen edge and the camera keeps moving. Drag pan holds a mouse button and drags the world. Both can be on at once.
useCases: An RTS or MOBA camera over a battlefield.
A city-builder or strategy map the player drags around.

params.tuning: In pixels, so it feels narrower on a high-density display. Around 10-20 is typical at 1080p.
Leave on for multi-monitor setups, or the camera keeps panning after the cursor leaves the game window.
The usual choice for a 3D top-down view. Turn it off for a 2D XY setup.
Without bounds the player can pan off the map entirely, which nearly always reads as a bug.

gotchas.title: Edge pan and drag pan can fight
gotchas.body: With both enabled, a drag that ends near the screen edge continues as an edge pan. Usually fine, occasionally surprising.

gotchas.title: Panning ignores terrain height
gotchas.body: It moves on a flat plane, so over tall terrain the camera can end up underground. Add your own height sampling if the map is not roughly flat.
